claims.label: async_cross_domain
claims.claim: The whitepaper minting sequence waits for six BTC confirmations before a custodian mints on Ethereum; its burning sequence waits for 25 Ethereum confirmations before BTC release and completion marking.

claims.label: async_cross_domain
claims.claim: That merchant/custodian workflow supplies linked transitions in Bitcoin and Ethereum with an explicit confirmation boundary. It satisfies the proposed predicate within this documented workflow; the rule does not require a trustless relay.

claims.label: async_cross_domain
claims.claim: The current FAQ summarizes merchant/custodian deposit and release but does not provide those numeric finality requirements. The historical-style whitepaper workflow is not asserted to be every current deployment or chain.

claims.label: legal_obligor
claims.claim: The whitepaper restricts burning to merchants and describes duties between custodians and merchants. The retained terms govern website use and information.

claims.label: legal_obligor
claims.claim: Those sources do not supply an applicable agreement naming the entity and legally grounded performance owed to an ordinary token holder. Merchant operational duties and informational website terms do not fill that gap.

qualifications: The supported proposal is limited to the whitepaper BTC/Ethereum merchant workflow; exact historical deployment and current confirmation policies remain unverified.

The current FAQ compresses release to the user, whereas the whitepaper separates merchant burning/release from the user exchange. This packet does not erase that scope difference or grant users merchant permissions.
The website terms identify their operator by a pronoun and govern website access. They are not a merchant custody agreement or ordinary-holder redemption contract.

No present custodian ownership structure, reserve sufficiency, licensing, legal enforceability or unconditional holder redemption right is verified. A legal-obligor gap is not a claim that no party has any legal obligation.
All three sources are one WBTC publisher family, not independent corroboration. No block explorer, reserve audit or on-chain execution was performed.
